Alice — thanks for the clear list. I'll answer briefly and attach a worked example. High level: we support two orthogonal controls you can combine: committed token bands (price per committed token, with true-up) and performance slots (reserved low-latency concurrency). Burst credits are a short-term buffer that let you exceed committed throughput without immediate overage charges; they have limited roll-forward.

Key bullets:
- Commit bands convert to baseline CPU/GPU capacity; we map expected 99th-pct latency by assigning performance slots where each slot targets one low-latency concurrent stream (approx).
- Formula: slots_needed = ceil(peak_concurrent_streams / slot_concurrency_factor). We'll provide a model in the attached workbook.
- Burst credits: generated monthly as a % of committed tokens (we typically use 15% by default on 12-mo commits), usable immediately, expire after 60 days (no indefinite roll-forward).
- True-up: any overage beyond burst + committed tokens billed at the overage rate on the invoice; we offer grace-bands for the first quarter with pro-rated credits on multi-year deals.

Ben will follow with the pricing numbers and example calc.

—Monica

Alice / FinShield team —

Attached is an example pricing sheet (FinShield_RFP_AppC_Pricing.xlsx) and a short summary here with numbers for a 12-month commit at list price $0.00030/token (base, pay-as-you-go). We can apply an initial 20% volume discount to committed tokens and separate per-slot reservation fees for low-latency capacity. Example:

Scenario A — 12-month, 250M committed tokens/month, 20% commit discount, performance needs: average 150 concurrent streams peak
- List PAYG token price: $0.00030 per token
- Committed token price (12-mo, 20% off): $0.00024 per token
- Monthly committed tokens: 250,000,000 -> committed spend = $60,000/month at committed rate
- Burst credits: 15% of committed tokens = 37,500,000 burst tokens/month (expire after 60 days)
- Slot model: slot_concurrency_factor = 8 (one slot ≈ supports 8 concurrent chat streams at targeted 99th-pct) -> slots_needed = ceil(150 / 8) = 19 slots
- Slot reservation fee: $2,500/slot/month (includes reserved GPU micro-instance + guaranteed KV-cache locality) -> slot fees = 19 * $2,500 = $47,500/month
- Overage rate (beyond committed + burst): $0.00042 per token (40% premium to list)

Example combined monthly cost (committed + slots) = $60,000 + $47,500 = $107,500 (excl. any overage). If you stay within committed + burst we bill committed rate only.

We also offer:
- Grace-band: first month of go-live we absorb 50% of overage up to 10% of committed tokens (useful for initial spikes).
- True-up cadence: monthly with consolidated quarter-end reconciliation if you prefer quarterly billing.
- Multi-year escalator: 3% annual rate increase baked into 2-yr deals; larger discounts for 36+ month contracts.

I'll add the cell-by-cell calculation in the workbook so you can swap inputs. Happy to run a tailored calc if you share an anonymized 3-month sample.

Monica / Ben —

Internal note for the record and for Procurement options: propose two alternate commercial structures in the RFP appendix so FinShield can choose by risk profile.

Option 1 (Commit-heavy, slot-reservation): best for predictable spend + latency guarantees
- Commit: 250M tokens/mo @ 20% discount
- Slots: pay per-slot reservation to cover 99th-pct latency
- Burst: 15% monthly, 60-day expiry
- True-up: monthly; grace-band first 90 days

Option 2 (Flexible blended): lower commit, larger burst buffer
- Commit: 150M tokens/mo @ 15% discount
- Slots: commit only for critical low-latency flows (e.g., 8 slots) and use elastic pool for non-critical
- Burst: 35% monthly, 30-day expiry
- Overage: tiered down to $0.00036/token for high-volume months if rolling 3-month avg > 200M

Additions to include in the appendix: examples of invoice line items, early termination pro-rata, and a short note on auditability (we provide per-token usage logs and request-level latency traces for compliance).

Alice / all — quick technical finance clarifications you may want to add to the procurement pack:

- Slot sizing: we determine slot_concurrency_factor empirically per-model. For your 2k-context chat model we use a conservative factor of 6-8 depending on quantization and batching. The workbook includes both scenarios — we recommend sizing to the 99th percentile observed concurrency from your sample.
- Token accounting: we count input+output tokens against committed buckets; streaming responses allocate tokens as generated (no pre-reservation).
- Burst credit accounting: consumed from oldest-to-newest committed bucket, and we show a ledger per-account in the console for audit.
- Invoice examples: we'll include a sample invoice line (committed tokens, slots, burst credit utilization, overage at premium) so your AP team sees line-by-line mapping.
